title: One Leaf, 2,000 Teas — China's Tea Secret | China Travel Expert
description:
Green, black, oolong, white — in China they all start from the SAME leaf. So what makes them different?

Every Chinese tea comes from one plant, Camellia sinensis. The category is decided by processing — mainly how long the leaf is oxidized: green tea is barely oxidized (fresh, grassy), black tea is fully oxidized (dark, sweet), and oolong sits in between. From six base categories, China makes over 2,000 different teas. In 2022, UNESCO added China's traditional tea-processing techniques to its Intangible Cultural Heritage list — an inscription covering 44 tea traditions across 15 provinces.

🧭 Expert Tip: In a Chinese teahouse, the first steep is usually a quick rinse to wake the leaves — pour it out and drink from the second steep.

一片叶子，两千多种茶——区别只在“氧化多久”。
